description: Given the root of a binary tree, construct a matrix to display it. The matrix has height rows and 2^height - 1 columns. Place the root at the middle of the first row, and recursively place children at the midpoints of their respective sections.
intuition: Think of the matrix as a complete binary tree layout. The root goes at the center column, and each child goes at the center of its half. Recursively dividing the column range in half for left and right children places every node at the correct position.
approach: First compute the tree height to determine dimensions. Then use DFS to place each node at the correct row and column position based on the formula.
explanation:
1. Compute the height of the tree to determine the matrix dimensions.
2. The matrix has height rows and 2^height - 1 columns.
3. Place each node at the midpoint of its column range.
4. Left child uses the left half, right child uses the right half.
hints: First compute the tree height to know the matrix size.
Each node goes at the midpoint of its available column range.
Recursively divide the column range for left and right children.
